designationHistory.indexText: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service established Ellicott Slough National Wildlife Refuge to protect the endangered Santa Cruz long-toed salamander.
designationHistory.note: The refuge page gives only the month or year. The refuge page does not say how it was established.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: Ellicott Slough National Wildlife Refuge, About Us

USFWS, Ellicott Slough National Wildlife Refuge: Final Comprehensive Conservation Plan and Environmental Assessment (ServCat 1418): "Established in 1975, the Refuge provides vital habitat for the endangered Santa Cruz long-toed salamander"

review.note: 1975 (CCP). Authority assumed ESA; exact date not found.

designationHistory.indexOriginal: The refuge, established in 1975 to protect the endangered Santa Cruz long-toed salamander, supports two of the 24 known breeding populations of the salamander.
